paper.title: Refined Lower Bounds for Adversarial Bandits

unmapped: losses in [0,1]^K; regret against best fixed arm in hindsight (realised regret R_T)
settings.definition_quote: The adversary then chooses a loss vector $\ell_t = (\ell_{i,t})_{1 \leq i \leq K} \in [0,1]^K$, which may depend on $p_t$. Finally the learner samples an action from $p_t$ denoted by $I_t$ and observes her own loss $\ell_{I_t,t}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial bandits on small-loss ball B_{alpha,T}
unmapped: losses in [0,1]; loss sequence restricted to L*_T/T <= alpha (first-order / small-loss ball)

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial bandits on small-variation ball V_{alpha,T}
unmapped: losses in [0,1]; loss sequence restricted to quadratic variation Q_T/(TK) <= alpha (second-order)

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial bandits with losses of small effective range C_rho
unmapped: each loss vector lies in C_rho = {x in [0,1]^K: max_{i,j}|x_i - x_j| <= rho} (effective range rho)

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial bandits with an arm optimal at every round
unmapped: losses in [0,1]; there exists an arm i* with l_{i*,t} = min_i l_{i,t} for all t
settings.definition_quote: there is a loss sequence $\ell_{1:T} \in [0,1]^{K T}$ such that there exists an arm $i^*$ that is optimal at every round~$t$ (i.e., $\ell_{i^*,t} = \min_i \ell_{i,t}$ for all~$t \geq 1$)

bound.regime: K >= 2, delta in (0,1/4), T >= 32(K-1)log(2/delta); holds with probability at least delta/2

extra_assumptions: loss sequence can be chosen with a single arm optimal in every round and per-round range at most sqrt((K-1)log(1/(4delta))/T)/(4 sqrt(log 2))

source.label: thm:high-prob
source.quote: Suppose $K \geq 2$ and $\delta \in (0,1/4)$ and $T \geq 32 (K-1) \log(2/\delta)$, then there exists a sequence of losses $\ell_{1:T} \in [0,1]^{KT}$ such that \Pr{R_T(\ell_{1:T}) \geq \frac{1}{27} \sqrt{(K-1)T \log(1/(4\delta))}} \geq \delta/2

results.notes: Regret exceeds the bound with probability >= delta/2 (not 1-delta).

bound.regime: K >= 2, delta in (0,1/4), sqrt((K-1)/T) log(1/(4delta)) <= C_alg, T >= 32 log(2/delta); holds with probability at least delta/2

symbols.C_alg: constant such that the strategy satisfies E[R_T] <= C_alg sqrt((K-1)T) for all loss sequences

extra_assumptions: strategy has expected regret at most C_alg sqrt((K-1)T) for every loss sequence

source.label: thm:high-prob-uniform
source.quote: Suppose $K \geq 2$, $T \geq 1$, and there exists a strategy and constant $C > 0$ such that for any $\ell_{1:T}$ it holds that $\E[R_T(\ell_{1:T})] \leq C \sqrt{(K-1)T}$. Let $\delta \in (0,1/4)$ satisfy $\sqrt{(K-1)/T} \log(1/(4\delta)) \leq C$ and $T \geq 32 \log(2/\delta)$. Then there exists $\ell_{1:T}$ for which \Pr{R_T(\ell_{1:T}) \geq \frac{\sqrt{(K-1)T}\log(1/(4\delta))}{203 C}} \geq \delta / 2

results.notes: Algorithm class: strategies with minimax-optimal expected regret C sqrt((K-1)T).

symbols.a_ball: Bernoulli parameter alpha of the optimal arm's losses in the construction

extra_assumptions: expectation also over random losses drawn from mixture of Bernoulli environments Q-bar

source.label: lem:firstorder-stochasticexample
source.quote: Let $\alpha \in (0,1)$, $K \geq 2$, and $T \geq K/(4(1-\alpha))$. Consider the probability distributions~$\Q_j$ ... with $\epsilon = (1/2) \sqrt{\alpha (1-\alpha) K/T}$, and set $\bar{\Q} = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{j=1}^K \Q_j$. Then for any randomised bandit algorithm $\E[\Reg_T(\ell_{1:T})] \geq \sqrt{\alpha (1-\alpha) T K} / 8$

results.notes: Lower bound against a randomized stochastic Bernoulli adversary; implies a worst-case bound over sequences.

bound.regime: K >= 2, T >= max(K,118), a_ball in [max(c log(32T), K/2)/T, 1/2], c=64/9

symbols.a_ball: radius alpha of small-loss ball: L*_T/T <= alpha

source.label: thm:firstorder-lowerbound
source.quote: Let $K \geq 2$, $T \geq K \vee 118$, and $\alpha \in \left[(c \log(32 T) \vee (K/2))/T, 1/2\right]$, where $c=64/9$. Then for any randomised bandit algorithm $\sup_{\ell_{1:T} \in \cB_{\alpha,T}} \E[\Reg_T(\ell_{1:T})] \geq \sqrt{\alpha T K} / 27$

results.notes: Equivalently sqrt(L*_T K) first-order lower bound.

symbols.a_ball: radius alpha of small-variation ball: Q_T/(TK) <= alpha

source.label: thm:variation-lowerbound
source.quote: Let $K \geq 2$, $T \geq (32 K) \vee 601$, and $\alpha \in [(2 c_1 \log(T) \vee 8K)/T, 1/4]$, where $c_1 = (4/9)^2 (3\sqrt{5}+1)^2 \leq 12$. Then for any randomised bandit algorithm, $\sup_{\ell_{1:T} \in \cV_{\alpha,T}} \E[\Reg_T(\ell_{1:T})] \geq \sqrt{\alpha T K} / 25$

symbols.rho: effective range of losses per round

source.label: thm:impossibility-result-1
source.quote: Let $K \geq 2$, $T \geq 32(K-1)\log(14)$ and $\rho \geq 0.22 \sqrt{(K-1)/T}$. Then for any randomised bandit algorithm, $\sup_{\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T \in \cC_{\rho}} \E[\Reg_T(\ell_{1:T})] \geq \sqrt{T (K-1)} / 504$

results.notes: Shows regret cannot scale with effective range.

source.label: thm:impossibility-result-2
source.quote: Let $K \geq 2$ and $T \geq 32(K-1)\log(14)$. Then, for any randomised bandit algorithm, there is a loss sequence $\ell_{1:T} \in [0,1]^{K T}$ such that there exists an arm $i^*$ that is optimal at every round~$t$ ..., but $\E[\Reg_T(\ell_{1:T})] \geq \sqrt{T (K-1)} / 504$
